reason: H0 is incompatible with S1's one-argument fpixCopy/dpixCopy API and, even after mechanical adaptation, its linear-combination calls use the now-invalid distinct-destination protocol. It therefore misses successful null-destination and in-place paths, newly accepted source aliasing and unequal-size semantics, and the changed destination protocols of the flip, rotation, and endian-swap functions.
evidence: S1 declares fpixCopy(FPIX *fpixs) and dpixCopy(DPIX *dpixs), while H0 repeatedly calls fpixCopy(NULL, fpix_payload) and dpixCopy(NULL, dpix_payload).
H0 calls dpixLinearCombination(dpix_copy6, dpix1, dpix2, 1.1, 1.2), where dpix_copy6 is distinct from dpix1; S1 rejects any dpixd where dpixd != dpixs1 as "invalid inplace operation".
H0 similarly calls fpixLinearCombination(fpix_copy3, fpix5, fpix6, 1.1, 1.1), so its only FPIX call is rejected before pixel processing.

S1 removes the fpixs1 == fpixs2 and dpixs1 == dpixs2 rejection and documents that the two sources need not have the same size, but H0 uses separate fixed-size 300x300 sources and does not vary aliasing or relative dimensions.
S1 changes fpixEndianByteSwap, dpixEndianByteSwap, fpixRotate180, fpixFlipLR, and fpixFlipTB to support only NULL destination or destination equal to source; H0 invokes none of these entry points.
recommended_action: Update H0 to the one-argument copy API, then fuzz linear combinations with destination NULL or equal to source1, source1/source2 aliasing, and independently varied dimensions. Add calls for endian swaps, rotate180, and LR/TB flips covering both NULL-destination and in-place protocols.
